Diarrhea or urethritis 2–4 weeks before the joint pain

red_flags: Single hot swollen joint with fever — septic arthritis until proven otherwise
Inability to move the joint or bear weight
Acute monoarthritis in a diabetic or immunosuppressed patient
Pain and fever in a joint with a prosthesis
Constitutional decline: weight loss, drenching night sweats
exam: Count and map every involved joint; note symmetry
Feel for warmth and effusion (patellar tap); note overlying erythema
Compare active and passive range of motion
Examine the hands: MCP/PIP synovitis, DIP Heberden nodes, deformities
Search for tophi on ears, elbows, and fingers
Inspect skin, scalp, and nails: psoriatic plaques, nail pitting, malar rash, oral ulcers
Look for dactylitis and Achilles/plantar enthesitis
Stress the sacroiliac joints and screen spinal movement
Record temperature; palpate for lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly

investigations.why: Marked leukocytosis supports septic arthritis; cytopenias support SLE; normal counts fit osteoarthritis and fibromyalgia
Separates inflammatory disease (RA, septic, brucellosis, SLE — raised) from mechanical osteoarthritis and fibromyalgia (normal)
Supports gout between attacks; may be normal during the acute attack, so it does not exclude it
Positive serology rules rheumatoid arthritis in when small joints are symmetrically involved > 6 weeks
Rules brucellosis in — a common cause of mono/oligoarthritis with undulant fever and raw-dairy exposure in Iraq
Joint-space narrowing and osteophytes rule osteoarthritis in; erosions support established RA or gout
The decisive test for any effusion: organisms on Gram stain/culture rule septic arthritis in; crystals rule gout in
Second-line — if photosensitive rash, oral ulcers, or cytopenias: supports SLE; ordered only with lupus features because a lone positive misleads
Proteinuria or hematuria flags renal involvement of SLE and separates it from uncomplicated joint disease
